Monstera deliciosa likes bright indirect light and will scorch in hours of direct afternoon sun. Water when the top few centimetres of soil are dry, then water thoroughly and let it drain; soggy soil causes root rot. It climbs in nature, so a moss pole encourages bigger leaves with more splits. Yellowing lower leaves often mean overwatering, brown crispy edges mean low humidity. Repot every couple of years into a chunky mix, see [[Potting mix for aroids]].
